purpose: Assessment-objective, command-word and paper-structure reference for the 9609 AS build. Read by the authoring and learning-item stages so that every note and every card carries an explicit AO and command-word intention.
authority: Extracted from the Cambridge 9609 syllabus v2 (2026-2028) via the frozen qualification profile. The profile remains the source of truth; this file adds the generation-facing mappings the profiles do not yet carry.

assessment_objectives.name: Knowledge and understanding
assessment_objectives.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of business concepts, terms and theories.

assessment_objectives.name: Application
assessment_objectives.description: Apply knowledge and understanding to problems and issues in familiar and unfamiliar business situations and contexts.

assessment_objectives.name: Analysis
assessment_objectives.description: Analyse qualitative and quantitative business information, causes, impacts and consequences; distinguish evidence from opinion; and draw valid inferences and generalisations.

assessment_objectives.name: Evaluation
assessment_objectives.description: Evaluate evidence to make reasoned judgements, present substantiated conclusions and, where appropriate, recommend action and implementation.

papers.name: Business Concepts 1
sections: Section A: four compulsory questions of five marks each; the first three questions have two parts.
Section B: answer one essay from a choice of two; each essay has two parts and totals 20 marks.
evaluation_locations: The second part of each Section B essay should show AO4 evaluation.

papers.name: Business Concepts 2
sections: Each question contains written, numerical, and/or diagrammatic stimulus and has six parts.
evaluation_locations: The last part of each question should show AO4 evaluation.

ao_mark_budget.arithmetic_note: Paper-level weights applied to paper marks give AO1 32, AO2 30, AO3 20, AO4 18 out of 100, against stated qualification weights of 30/30/20/20. A two-mark divergence on AO1 and AO4. Cambridge publishes both figures and rounding across two papers explains it, but authoring should target the stated 30/30/20/20 rather than the derived split.

command_words.a_credit_worthy_answer: One canonical sentence giving precise meaning. No example required, no evaluation.
command_words.evidence_note: AS: always 2 marks. Paper 1 Section A part (a).

command_words.a_credit_worthy_answer: Name or select. Nothing beyond naming earns credit.
command_words.evidence_note: AS: always 1 mark. Paper 1 Section A part (i), Paper 2 part (a)(i).

command_words.meaning: Set out purposes or reasons, make relationships clear, say why and/or how, and support with relevant evidence.
command_words.a_credit_worthy_answer: State the point, give the reason or mechanism, make the relationship clear, and support with evidence from the context.
command_words.evidence_note: AS: always 3 marks. The most common command word at AS - 147 of 988 parts.
command_words.syllabus_verbatim: Explain set out purposes or reasons / make the relationships between things clear / say why and/or how and support with relevant evidence

command_words.meaning: Work out from given facts, figures or information.
command_words.a_credit_worthy_answer: Formula, substitution, answer with correct units, then one sentence of interpretation.
command_words.evidence_note: AS: always 3 marks. Paper 2 only, always with 'Refer to Fig./Table'.
command_words.syllabus_verbatim: Calculate work out from given facts, figures or information

command_words.meaning: Examine in detail to show meaning, identify elements and the relationship between them.
command_words.a_credit_worthy_answer: A chain: decision or condition -> immediate effect -> mechanism -> measurable consequence -> effect on an objective or stakeholder. Conditional language, no jump straight to profit.
command_words.evidence_note: AS: 8 marks as Section B part (a) or Paper 2 part (c); 5 marks as Paper 1 Section A question 4.
command_words.syllabus_verbatim: Analyse examine in detail to show meaning, identify elements and the relationship between them

command_words.a_credit_worthy_answer: Weigh significance rather than list both sides, name the decisive criterion, and reach a supported judgement.
command_words.evidence_note: NOT USED AT AS. Zero occurrences in 84 AS papers 2020-2025. Appears in the syllabus command-word list because the list covers Papers 3 and 4 as well.

command_words.meaning: Judge or calculate the quality, importance, amount or value of something.
command_words.a_credit_worthy_answer: Judgement + specific context + decisive criterion and reason + strongest counterargument + condition for success. 'It depends' without saying what it depends on scores nothing.
command_words.evidence_note: AS: always 12 marks, as the second part of a Section B essay or the final part of a Paper 2 question. The 20-mark figure in the syllabus is the WHOLE Section B question (8 + 12), not the Evaluate part.
command_words.syllabus_verbatim: Evaluate judge or calculate the quality, importance, amount, or value of something

command_words.meaning: Support a case with evidence or argument.
command_words.a_credit_worthy_answer: Support one case with evidence and argument, and say why the rejected options are weaker.
command_words.evidence_note: RETIRED AT AS. 22 occurrences 2020-2022, zero from 2023. Do not generate AS items for it.
command_words.syllabus_verbatim: Justify support a case with evidence/argument

command_words.meaning: Write down a suggested course of action in a given situation.
command_words.a_credit_worthy_answer: A specific recommended course of action for this business, with the criterion behind it and the conditions under which it succeeds.
command_words.evidence_note: NOT USED AT AS. Zero occurrences in 84 AS papers 2020-2025. A Level only.
command_words.syllabus_verbatim: Advise write down a suggested course of action in a given situation

flashcard_subtype_ao_map.note: The default card. A deck that is mostly DEF cards fails the qualification profile.

flashcard_subtype_ao_map.tests: Boundary between two easily confused concepts
Purpose or reason something exists or is done
The mechanism by which a cause produces an effect
A developed benefit, not a listed one
A developed limitation, not a listed one
The concept used in a business context whose facts change the answer
A full analysis chain to a measurable consequence
A judgement with a decisive criterion and a counterargument
What a figure, chart or result means for the business
A common error, stated and corrected
A link across two or more topics

item_mix_target.principle: A topic's learning-item set should distribute across AOs in roughly the qualification's own proportions. Seventy per cent of this qualification lies beyond AO1, so a deck that is mostly definitions is not a light version of the resource - it is the wrong resource.
hard_rules: Every major objective (depth tier 3 or 4) carries at least one APP item with context facts that change the reasoning.
Every objective whose command words include Analyse carries at least one CHAIN item.
Every objective whose command words include Evaluate carries at least one EVAL item. Assess, Advise and Justify are not generated for AS - they are not used in AS papers.
Every quantitative objective carries a CALC item and an INTERP item; a calculation without interpretation is incomplete under RS-22.
AO1-only subtypes must not exceed the AO1 target share of a topic's item set.

AO4 is measured in practice time, not item count. Every AO4-bearing objective carries at least one evaluation item; the AO4 share is met by essay plans, data-response tasks and case analyses, not by multiplying EVAL flashcards.
Generate AS items only for the six command words actually used at AS: Identify, Define, Explain, Calculate, Analyse, Evaluate.
Coverage floor: an objective classed unprobed_2020_2025 still receives DEF and DIST items and joins synoptic mixed practice. Exposure changes item type, never item presence.
item_mix_target.correction_2026_08_31: AO1, AO2 and AO3 shares govern the flashcard and short-answer bank. AO4 is carried by a smaller number of high-value performance items - essay plans, data-response tasks, case analyses. The deterministic check becomes: every objective carrying AO4 has at least one evaluation item, AND AO4 practice time is at least 20% of total practice time - not 20% of item count.

paper_structure_verified.verified_against: Syllabus v2 section 4 'Details of the assessment', cross-checked against all 21 Paper 1 and 21 Paper 2 papers from 2023-2025.

paper_1.section_a: Four compulsory questions of 5 marks each. Questions 1-3 have two parts (2 + 3). Question 4 is a single 5-mark Analyse part.
paper_1.section_b: Two essay questions of 20 marks each; candidates answer one. Each has two parts: (a) Analyse 8 marks, (b) Evaluate 12 marks.

paper_2.structure: Two compulsory 30-mark data-response questions, six parts each: (a)(i) Identify 1, (a)(ii) Explain 3, (b)(i) Calculate 3, (b)(ii) Explain 3, (c) Analyse 8, (d) Evaluate 12.
paper_2.confirmed_in: 42 of 42 questions 2023-2025 total exactly 30 marks in exactly 6 parts

paper_structure_verified.note: The 20-mark and 30-mark figures in the syllabus are QUESTION totals. Command-word tariffs above are PART tariffs. Both are correct; the earlier report did not distinguish them clearly.

calibration_window.reason: The 2023 revision changed the command-word set. 'Discuss' appears 64 times in 2020-2022 and never after; Evaluate rises from 19 to 84; Identify appears from nothing; Justify disappears. Paper 1 Section B also carried a third essay option (question 7) in the older papers.

revision_note: Revised after Stage 4 mining. Estimated tariff ranges replaced by measured exact values; Assess, Advise and Justify removed from AS generation; calibration window restricted to 2023-2025; paper structure verified.

exam_exposure.principle: Exposure is evidence metadata, never a priority ranking. RS-05 forbids frequency removing or weakening syllabus-mandated coverage.
exam_exposure.coverage_floor: Every mandatory objective receives at least a DEF and a DIST item regardless of exposure. Nobody gets zero.
exam_exposure.review_set: rarely-examined - a filtered view over the one item bank, per RS-26. Not a chapter, not a duplicate bank.

blooms_taxonomy.why_both: The assessment objective says what the examination credits. The Bloom level says what the learner is being asked to do. They are different axes and an item carries both.

levels.means: Recall a fact, a term or a list, as stated.
Explain an idea in the learner’s own words, or tell it apart from a neighbouring one.
Use the idea on a case, a figure or a diagram the learner has not been given the answer to.
Break a situation into its parts and trace a cause through to its consequence for a named party.
Weigh two sides against a criterion and reach a judgement that could have gone the other way.
Build something new from the parts. Rare below A Level; used here only for extended performance tasks that ask a learner to design or plan.

blooms_taxonomy.depth_lift: A Remember or Understand subtype on a depth-tier 4 objective is lifted one level.

provenance_rule: Every value carries one of three provenances. "syllabus" is transcribed from the named page. "corpus" is counted from the published papers. "judgement" is our reading. Nothing here is written from recall.
enrichment_note: Provenance, Bloom’s taxonomy and references to the answer-shape, misconception and exclusion files added. AO weights, mark budget and tariffs are unchanged: they were checked against the syllabus and passed.
